report.summary: An incident affecting payments and ledger services started at 13:06 on 2026-10-17 when database statement timeouts began occurring due to table lock contention. Specifically, the daily reconciliation cron job on ledger-db acquired a share row exclusive lock on the ledger_entries table at 13:04, blocking incoming transactional inserts and causing widespread active connection pile-ups, latency spikes, and 10-second statement timeouts starting at 13:05/13:06.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Daily reconciliation cron job table lock contention on ledger-db

supporting.note: ledger-db cron job executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries at 13:04:02, directly preceding the anomaly.
Continuous warnings starting at 13:05 for processes waiting for RowExclusiveLock on ledger_entries.
Ledger-db latency spiked upward starting at 13:05.
Ledger-db active connections surged starting at 13:05.
Ledger-service statements timed out on INSERT INTO ledger_entries starting at 13:06.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Payments-api logging configuration change causing thread pool or serialization overhead

supporting.note: Config change on payments-api at 13:02 setting ledger client logging to DEBUG.

contradicting.note: Actual failures are database statement timeouts inside ledger-db and ledger-service, not client-side formatting delays.
ledger-db explicitly started its blocking table lock at 13:04, establishing an independent database-side cause.

facts.text: payments-api error_rate_pct and latency_p99_ms started an upward anomaly at 2026-10-17T13:06:00+00:00.
ledger-service error_rate_pct and latency_p99_ms started an upward anomaly at 2026-10-17T13:06:00+00:00 (and 13:05 for p99 latency).
payments-api logs show persistent errors: ledger-service POST /entries timed out after 10s starting at 13:06:02.
ledger-service logs show persistent statement timeouts: INSERT INTO ledger_entries canceled after 10000 ms starting at 13:06:04.
At 2026-10-17T13:04:02, ledger-db started a cron job reconcile_daily which executed LOCK TABLE ledger_entries IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE.
Ledger-db latency_p99_ms showed an upward anomaly starting at 13:05, jumping from ~15 ms to a peak of 10527.28 ms.
Ledger-db active connections showed an upward anomaly starting at 13:05, surging from ~45 to ~180 active connections.
Starting at 13:05, ledger-db logged continuous warnings of processes waiting for RowExclusiveLock on the ledger_entries relation.

assumptions: The reconcile_daily cron job holds the table lock for the duration of the reconciliation process, blocking concurrent writes.

timeline.event: payments-api config change chg-9660 applied (logging.ledger_client set to DEBUG)
ledger-db cron job reconcile_daily started with LOCK TABLE ledger_entries IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE
ledger-db processes begin waiting for RowExclusiveLock and active connections/latency spike
Upstream error and latency anomalies start on payments-api and ledger-service due to database statement timeouts

recommended_actions.action: Optimize or reschedule the reconcile_daily cron job on ledger-db to avoid blocking concurrent transactional writes on ledger_entries during peak traffic hours.
recommended_actions.rationale: The daily cron job acquires a broad table lock that causes cascading statement timeouts and connection pool exhaustion.

recommended_actions.action: Implement more granular locking strategies or MVCC-compliant queries for reconciliation tasks.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevent exclusive table locks from halting regular INSERT and UPDATE statements on ledger tables.
